newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS BEAT BRUINS IN LEMIEUX'S LAST HOME GAME.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PENGUINS BEAT BRUINS IN LEMIEUX'S LAST HOME GAME.

text.p: Patrick Lalime made 38 saves and Petr Nedved and Ed Olczyk each had a goal and an assist as the Penguins extended their unbeaten streak to five games with a 3-1 victory over the Boston Bruins in Mario Lemieux's final regular-season home game.

Lemieux, who said last weekend that his 12th NHL season would be his last, picked up an assist on Olczyk's empty-net goal. Lemieux leads the league with 118 points -- Anaheim's Teemu Selanne is second with 106 points -- and will capture his sixth scoring title at the conclusion of the season.

"I was a little nervous at the beginning," Lemieux said. "I think it showed, I pressed a little on a couple of shots. It's always great at the end of a career to get the recognition. It was really something to receive the standing ovations."
Landon Wilson had the lone goal for Boston.
At Tampa Bay, Jay Pandolfo's goal 2:11 into the third period lifted the New Jersey Devils into a 2-2 tie with the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Martin Brodeur made 37 saves for New Jersey, which allowed a season-high 39 shots on goal. John MacLean scored a goal for the fourth consecutive game to account for the Devils' other goal.

The Devils, who are 5-0-1 in their last six games, have 102 points and lead the Philadelphia Flyers for first place in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference by two points with three games to play.
Jason Wiemer and Cory Cross scored for Tampa Bay, which is three points behind the Hartford Whalers for the eighth and final spot in the Eastern Conference.
In Calgary, Tomas Sandstrom scored with nine seconds left in overtime to lift the Detroit Red Wings to a 3-2 victory over the Flames, severely damaging Calgary's playoff hopes.
Steve Yzerman scored twice for Detroit. The Red Wings have already clinched third place in the Western Conference.
Ronnie Stern and Corey Millen scored for the Flames. Calgary trails the final playoff spot by four points with road games left against Chicago and Toronto.
